cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg23.txt <<'EOF'
fix(builtins): a by-ref parameter the call omitted is not an argument that cannot be passed

`stream_socket_client("unix://…", error_message: $why)` was refused with php's own words —
"Argument #2 ($error_code) could not be passed by reference" — for an argument the program never
wrote. The named argument skips `$error_code`, normalization materialises that parameter's `null`
default into the slot, and the by-reference check reads the NORMALIZED list, where a default the
compiler synthesised and a literal the programmer typed are the same expression.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6, and the two halves are what draw the line:

  - omitted is fine — skipped by a named argument, or trailing-omitted: `stream_socket_client(…)`
    with no error pair at all is accepted, and `str_replace("a","b","banana",$n)` sets `$n`.
  - written is an Error — `stream_socket_client("tcp://…", 0, $errstr, 1)` raises php's message,
    and an explicit `null` there raises exactly the same one. So the cases cannot be told apart by
    VALUE, only by provenance.

The plan already records it as `PlannedRegularArg::Default`; it just never reached the check. It
does now, and nothing else moves — an unmarked slot is still checked, so the direction of any
future gap is toward refusing, not toward accepting.

`test_out_parameter_rejects_an_argument_without_storage` asserted "parameter $error_code must be
passed a variable", which is neither php's wording nor what elephc emits — php says "Argument #2
($error_code) could not be passed by reference", which is what elephc already produced and what
the test now pins. The property it guards, that a literal in a by-ref slot is refused, is
unchanged and was re-measured rather than assumed.

`flock()`'s would-block output was written as a RAW word into a slot that may hold a boxed value.
An UNDECLARED `$would_block` — and `flock($h, LOCK_SH, $would)` is how php programs write it — gets
a `mixed` slot holding a boxed null, and the integer stored over that box pointer read back as
NULL where php answers `int(0)`. The socket builtins already write their by-reference integers
through `store_int_output_to_local`, which boxes for a `mixed` slot and REFUSES a slot that can
hold neither; `flock` was the last one doing it by hand, and kept its own copy of a bug the others
no longer had.

STILL DIVERGENT, measured here and not fixed: `flock()` answers `true` on `php://memory`,
`php://temp` and `php://stdout`, where php answers `false` for all three — php only locks a plain
FILE stream, and elephc backs a memory stream with a real `tmpfile()` descriptor that libc is happy
to lock. The wrapper kind is recorded per stream and keyed by the opaque HANDLE, which `flock` does
not currently carry; the out-parameter half is correct either way, since php writes `0` there
whatever its verdict.

`io::streams` goes from 14 failures to 11.
EOF
